query: How can businesses improve Yelp user satisfaction?

per_column.name: staff_conduct
per_column.rationale: Staff behavior is an intervenable lever a business can train and change; plausibly affects satisfaction.

per_column.name: value_perception
per_column.rationale: Pricing/value is a configurable business decision that can be set or changed, and influences satisfaction.

per_column.name: atmosphere_ambiance_signal
per_column.rationale: Ambiance (noise, decor, seating) is settable via renovation/design choices; an intervenable lever affecting satisfaction.

per_column.name: visit_context
per_column.rationale: Visit type (special event, first-time, late night) is not chosen by the business and can affect both what the business emphasizes and baseline satisfaction; it is a common-cause context, not a lever the business sets.

per_column.name: business_category
per_column.rationale: Category (restaurant, hotel, salon) is a common cause: it shapes which levers (staff, pricing, ambiance) are relevant and drives baseline satisfaction. Not intervenable in a what-if for a given business.

judge.rationale: The query asks how businesses can improve satisfaction, an interventional what-if. Multiple added columns are genuine intervenable levers a business could set or change (staff conduct, pricing/value, ambiance), satisfying the treatment-intervenability requirement. Two additional columns (business_category, visit_context) are plausible confounders: common causes influencing both which levers matter and baseline satisfaction, neither of which is named or implied in the query. business_category is the stronger confounder since it drives both applicable levers and satisfaction; visit_context is somewhat weaker and borderline could act as an effect modifier, but reasonably serves as an unnamed adjustment variable. This realises the what-if claim reasonably well.
